CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath. She reports experiencing palpitations and dyspnea with mild exertion, including walking up her driveway. Onset is unclear but she notes the episodes are occurring more frequently lately. She is uncertain whether this is related to her chronic back pain. She has recently increased her exercise regimen to lose weight from the COVID-19 pandemic. Notably, she has significantly reduced her smoking from 2 packs per day to approximately 1 cigarette per day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Completed by nursing staff. Patient denies other concerning symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Depression
- Chronic back pain
- Smoking history

MEDICATIONS
- Effexor (for depression)
- Gabapentin/Neurontin (for chronic back pain)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Smoking: Previously 2 packs per day, now reduced to approximately 1 cigarette per day. Currently exercising more frequently to address COVID-19 related weight gain. Previously discussed doing yoga but has not established this as a regular habit.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Unremarkable. Lungs: Mild wheezes noted in all lung fields.

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests: Findings consistent with asthma or COPD.
Chest X-ray: Flattened diaphragm noted, consistent with COPD changes seen in smokers.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): Newly diagnosed. Patient started on Combivent inhaler 2 puffs twice daily for airway maintenance. Albuterol inhaler 2 puffs as needed prescribed as rescue therapy. Prednisone taper pack prescribed.
2. Depression: Currently stable on Effexor. Continue current medication without changes.
3. Chronic back pain: Continue Gabapentin/Neurontin. Encouraged to incorporate yoga for pain and mood management.
